paragraphs: Diffusion language models reconstruct missing tokens using context from both directions, but their likelihood estimates and generated text have lagged behind autoregressive models. This paper identifies an explanation: masking important words early removes information that helps reconstruct the rest of a sentence. These words serve as anchors for other predictions.

The proposed Anchored Diffusion Language Model separates prediction into two stages. An anchor network first estimates distributions over important tokens. The second stage predicts missing tokens using those anchor predictions as context. The authors also derive an anchored training objective and theoretically show improvements in sample complexity and likelihood modeling.

Experiments report test-perplexity gains of up to 25.4% over earlier diffusion models on LM1B and OpenWebText, alongside strong zero-shot results across seven benchmarks. The model also exceeds autoregressive models on MAUVE, supporting a text-quality advantage on that measure. Additional results show benefits from anchoring autoregressive models and improvements over existing chain-of-thought approaches on math and logic tasks.
neurips-2025-anchored-diffusion-language.tldr: Predicting important anchor tokens first improves diffusion language modeling and also benefits autoregressive generation and reasoning.

paragraphs: Speech quality cannot be captured by a single score. Measures such as PESQ, STOI, and MOS describe different perceptual or objective aspects, and their scales and assumptions differ. ARECHO addresses the challenge of predicting several such measures together while accounting for relationships among them.

The system first converts speech information into tokens. A dynamic classifier chain then estimates metrics through an autoregressive process, explicitly modeling dependencies between predictions. A two-step decoding procedure uses confidence to improve reliability and reduce the propagation of errors through that chain. This makes the relationships between scores part of the evaluation mechanism rather than leaving each prediction isolated.

The authors report significant improvements over their baseline across enhanced, generated, and noisy speech evaluation. ARECHO works without a reference recording and supports requests for either individual metrics or selected groups of metrics. Its dependency modeling also improves interpretability by exposing relationships among measures, making the framework useful for examining several aspects of speech within one evaluation system.
neurips-2025-arecho-autoregressive-evalu.tldr: ARECHO jointly estimates speech metrics through a dynamic prediction chain that models their dependencies and uses confidence to reduce errors.

paragraphs: Language models can absorb gender biases from their training text. Changing their parameters to reduce those biases requires resources and access that closed-source models may not provide. Instructions offer another route, but the paper identifies a practical tension: instructions intended to reduce bias can also hurt performance on ordinary tasks.

FaIRMaker addresses this tension through automated search and refinement of instructions called Fairwords. It expands the space of candidate instructions and trains a sequence-to-sequence model to refine them adaptively. For gender-related queries, the resulting instructions aim to reduce bias; for neutral inputs, they aim to improve task performance.

This design places the adaptation in an instruction-generating framework that can work across models, including those whose parameters are inaccessible. The reported experiments find that FaIRMaker mitigates gender bias while preserving task integrity in both open- and closed-source language models. The contribution is therefore an adaptive way to combine bias mitigation with useful responses, rather than applying the same intervention indiscriminately to every query.
neurips-2025-auto-search-and-refinement-.tldr: FaIRMaker automatically searches for and refines instructions that reduce gender bias while preserving performance on ordinary tasks.

paragraphs: Combining cameras, LiDAR, and 4D radar improves object detection for autonomous driving, but the combination becomes fragile when a sensor degrades or fails. The paper identifies two difficulties: tightly coupled systems assume sensors remain available, while attention-based alternatives can be expensive and struggle to represent different sensors consistently.

Availability-aware sensor fusion addresses both issues with a shared feature representation and a cross-sensor attention mechanism. Unified canonical projection makes features from different sensors consistent for fusion. Cross-attention across sensors along patches then supports robustness when some sensor information deteriorates or disappears. Together, these components connect representation alignment with handling changes in sensor availability.

Experiments on K-Radar report stronger detection than existing state-of-the-art fusion methods under various weather and sensor degradation or failure conditions, with low computational cost. At an overlap threshold of 0.5, the abstract reports bird's-eye-view average precision of 87.2% and 3D average precision of 73.6%, with improvements stated as 9.7% and 20.1%, respectively. These findings support the approach in the evaluated conditions.
neurips-2025-availability-aware-sensor-f.tldr: A shared feature space and patch-based cross-sensor attention improve object detection when driving sensors degrade or fail.

paragraphs: BecomingLit reconstructs head avatars that can be animated, viewed from new angles, and illuminated differently at interactive rendering rates. The work begins with a low-cost light-stage setup designed for faces. It supplies a new dataset containing multiple viewpoints, changing illumination, and varied expressions across numerous subjects.

The avatar representation uses 3D Gaussian primitives, animated through a parametric head model and an expression-dependent dynamics module. Its shading combines a learned diffuse material response with an analytical specular term. This hybrid design supports separating material properties from the lighting observed during capture, which is central to rendering the same face under new illumination.

The resulting avatars support all-frequency relighting with point lights and environment maps, and monocular videos can control their animation. On the authors' dataset, experiments report substantial improvements over existing state-of-the-art methods for relighting and reenactment. The contribution connects capture, representation, animation, and shading into a system for preserving a reconstructed face while changing how it moves and how it is lit.
neurips-2025-becominglit-relightable-gau.tldr: BecomingLit combines facial light-stage capture, Gaussian avatars, and hybrid shading to enable interactive animation and relighting.

paragraphs: LiDAR semantic segmentation assigns categories to points in a 3D scene, and adapting this ability across domains remains difficult. BeyondMix argues that existing mixing-based approaches underuse the structure of point clouds. It focuses on three properties: invariance to point ordering, consistency within local regions, and consistency of geometry.

The framework uses Mamba state space models to incorporate these structural properties while modeling relationships over long distances. Space-filling curves turn the point cloud into ordered sequences, and spatial partitioning schemes help organize how its structure is processed. This gives the method a way to capture dependencies beyond the limited receptive fields of conventional voxel-based approaches.

The goal is to learn representations that remain useful across domains by combining structural knowledge with broader spatial context. Experiments on challenging LiDAR segmentation benchmarks report consistent improvements over existing state-of-the-art methods for unsupervised domain adaptation. These results support treating point-cloud organization as a central part of adaptation, alongside the model's ability to connect distant parts of a scene.
neurips-2025-beyondmix-leveraging-struct.tldr: BeyondMix combines point-cloud structural properties with Mamba-based long-range modeling to improve unsupervised LiDAR segmentation adaptation.

paragraphs: Climate simulators describe interacting Earth-system processes through coupled equations, but running them is computationally expensive. Machine learning offers a way to emulate their outputs more quickly. This paper targets a gap in that approach: incorporating causal relationships grounded in physical understanding into the learned emulator.

The authors develop an interpretable emulator based on causal representation learning. Its approach includes a Bayesian filter designed to support stable long-term autoregressive emulation. In this setting, the model repeatedly uses its evolving predictions to continue the simulated trajectory, making stability across successive steps an important part of the problem.

The evaluation uses both a realistic synthetic dataset and data from two widely deployed climate models. The authors report accurate learned climate dynamics and show that each component contributes to the approach. The findings connect two objectives that matter for emulation: representing causal structure and maintaining useful behavior over long sequences. The demonstrated scope is emulating the evaluated climate-model data, where the method provides an interpretable alternative to purely predictive modeling.
neurips-2025-causal-climate-emulation-wi.tldr: A causal climate emulator uses Bayesian filtering to learn interpretable dynamics and support stable long-term predictions.

paragraphs: Some Gaussian-splatting head generators condition their latent representation on camera position to stabilize training and improve difficult views. The paper observes that this can change the generated person's identity when the camera moves. Simply removing that conditioning can destabilize training, while fixing one viewpoint compromises rendering from other angles.

CGS-GAN addresses these problems with a generator that does not rely on view conditioning. A multi-view regularization method supports convergence with little computational overhead. The framework also adapts an existing conditional loss and introduces an architecture intended to combine stable training, efficient rendering, and scaling to resolutions of 2048 by 2048.

The authors additionally curate an FFHQ-derived dataset that includes larger portions of the head, supports high resolution, reduces view-dependent artifacts, and excludes subjects obscured by objects such as hands. They report high rendering quality with competitive FID scores and consistent 3D scene generation. The contribution is the combination of training changes and data preparation that lets camera movement reveal a consistent generated head.
neurips-2025-cgs-gan-3d-consistent-gauss.tldr: CGS-GAN stabilizes Gaussian-splatting head generation without camera conditioning, supporting consistent identities across views at high resolution.

paragraphs: Answering questions about hour-long videos requires finding relevant information within extensive visual and temporal content. Even language models with long-context capabilities can struggle with this density. Deep Video Discovery addresses the problem by treating video understanding as an adaptive search over segmented clips.

The DVD agent receives search-oriented tools operating on a video database organized at multiple levels of detail. It uses its current observations to plan what to inspect and select the next tool. As evidence accumulates, the workflow can change to fit the question. This makes the search process responsive to what the agent has already learned.

Evaluations across multiple long-video benchmarks show advantages for the approach. On LVBench, the agent reaches 74.2% accuracy, reported as state of the art, and reaches 76.0% when transcripts are available. These results support the value of combining language-model reasoning with selective access to video evidence. The transcript result also shows that additional textual information improves performance in that evaluated setting.
neurips-2025-deep-video-discovery-agenti.tldr: DVD adaptively searches segmented videos with tools, achieving strong long-video question-answering results that improve further with transcripts.

paragraphs: Linear structural causal models represent relationships among random variables using two kinds of edges. Directed edges describe direct causal effects, while bidirected edges represent hidden confounding. The paper studies generic identification: determining causal parameters from observed correlations within this modeling framework.

The general identification problem remains open, so the work focuses on a structured case in which the directed edges form a tree. An earlier result solved this case with a randomized polynomial-time algorithm requiring O(n^6) time. The new algorithm improves the stated running time to O(n^3 log² n), substantially reducing how quickly its computational requirements grow with problem size.

The authors also implement the algorithm and report that it outperforms existing state-of-the-art implementations. This supplies practical evidence alongside the improved complexity bound. The contribution is a faster solution for the tree-shaped case, with hidden confounders still represented by bidirected edges. Its scope remains generic identification in these linear models; the abstract does not extend the result to arbitrary directed causal structures.
neurips-2025-faster-generic-identificati.tldr: A faster algorithm reduces generic identification time for tree-shaped linear causal models from O(n^6) to O(n^3 log² n).

paragraphs: Contrastive pretraining learns representations that align related inputs, including inputs from different modalities. This paper studies the sigmoid loss used in SigLIP and SigLIP2, focusing on the role of jointly trainable inverse temperature and bias. Its goal is to explain how these parameters interact with representation geometry.

The authors introduce a family of geometric configurations called constellations, parameterized by a margin and a relative bias. These objects are related to spherical codes. For a rich class of such configurations, temperature and bias can drive the loss toward zero. This characterization describes a range of representation arrangements compatible with very small loss.

The theory is used to explain SigLIP's retrieval success, its modality gap, and the dimension needed for high-quality representations. The authors also propose rewriting the loss so that relative bias becomes an explicit parameter. Synthetic-data experiments show improved training dynamics with that formulation. The work therefore connects an analysis of possible minimizing configurations to a concrete change in how the loss is parameterized.
neurips-2025-global-minimizers-of-sigmoi.tldr: A geometric analysis explains how trainable temperature and bias shape sigmoid contrastive representations and motivates an improved loss parameterization.

paragraphs: Adversarial patches expose weaknesses in neural networks through localized changes to an input. Designing them involves several coupled choices: shape, location, number, and visual content. The paper argues that optimizing these factors separately restricts attack effectiveness because their combinations create a difficult joint search problem.

IMPACT provides a gradient-free framework for searching over these factors together. A reduced-dimensional encoding lowers computational complexity while retaining expressive power. Its first optimization phase uses differential evolution to jointly adjust the patch mask and content. A second phase uses an evolutionary strategy to refine the content more precisely after that broader search.

The framework also includes an aggregation procedure that merges localized regions into contiguous, irregular patches to support physical applicability. Experiments report significant improvements over several state-of-the-art approaches. The results highlight the benefit of considering patch configuration and content jointly, with the two phases organizing the search into broad composition followed by refinement. The abstract's physical-applicability claim concerns the construction of contiguous patches.
neurips-2025-impact-irregular-multi-patc.tldr: IMPACT jointly optimizes adversarial patch shape, placement, number, and content through a compact encoding and two gradient-free search phases.

paragraphs: Multi-view clustering groups samples using information from several sources or modalities, even when some observations are missing. Many methods learn a separate representation for each view and combine them afterward. This paper instead starts from the assumption that each sample has one latent representation shared across all its views.

Neural networks map that shared representation into each view's feature space. These mappings reconstruct observations that are available and fill in observations that are missing. An alignment measure then incorporates pairwise similarities across the observations, including the imputed ones. The authors describe this alignment computation as having linear complexity.

Reconstruction and alignment run iteratively, allowing the method to learn representations that distinguish samples for clustering. Standard clustering algorithms can then group those representations into categories. Benchmark experiments report state-of-the-art performance. The approach matters because missing views participate in the representation-learning process through imputation and alignment, rather than simply being absent from it. Its central modeling assumption is that the different views of a sample can share the same underlying latent representation.
neurips-2025-incomplete-multi-view-deep-.tldr: A shared latent representation supports iterative missing-view imputation and alignment, improving clustering across incomplete multi-view data.

paragraphs: Representing an environment as separate objects can help a reinforcement-learning agent organize what it observes. However, the paper argues that many object-centric methods leave interactions between objects implicit. FIOC-WM makes those interactions an explicit, structured part of a learned world model.

Using pretrained vision encoders, the framework learns object representations and an interaction structure directly from pixels. It models dynamics through modular, disentangled interaction representations and decomposes tasks into composable interaction primitives. A hierarchical policy then uses this structure: its high level selects which interactions to perform and in what order, while its low level carries them out.

On simulated robotics and embodied-AI benchmarks, the framework improves policy-learning sample efficiency and generalization relative to world-model baselines. These results support the value of explicitly learning reusable interactions alongside object representations. The proposed structure links perception, prediction, and action selection: objects organize the scene, interaction primitives organize possible changes, and the policy organizes how those changes should be executed to accomplish a task.
neurips-2025-learning-interactive-world-.tldr: FIOC-WM explicitly models objects and modular interactions, enabling hierarchical policies with improved sample efficiency and generalization in simulation.

paragraphs: Learning an image probability model is difficult because images occupy a high-dimensional space. This paper develops a way to learn normalized energy models, connecting an explicit log-probability representation with the score-estimation approach used in diffusion models. The network is adapted to output an energy while retaining the original architecture's inductive biases.

Differentiating that energy with respect to the input image gives the learned density's score, which is trained with a denoising objective. Differentiating with respect to noise level supplies a second score and a second training objective. This dual construction ensures that energies remain consistent and normalized across noise levels.

On ImageNet64, the method achieves negative log likelihood comparable to the state of the art. Networks trained on non-overlapping subsets also produce nearly identical log-probability estimates, which the authors present as strong generalization. Further analysis finds substantial content-dependent variation in image probabilities and local neighborhood dimensionality, challenging conventional assumptions about concentration or uniformly low-dimensional support in this setting.
neurips-2025-learning-normalized-image-d.tldr: Dual score matching learns normalized image probabilities by training an energy network through both image and noise-level derivatives.

paragraphs: Machine unlearning is often proposed as a response to problematic information in generative models, including concerns involving privacy, copyright, and safety. This paper examines what such proposals are actually asking a system to do and whether available implementations match those goals.

It distinguishes two objectives. One is removing the effects of particular information from a model's parameters, such as a person's data or copyrighted training material. The other is preventing outputs that contain targeted information, resemble particular data, or express a specified concept. These objectives concern different aspects of a model: what training has left inside it and what it produces when used.

The authors provide a framework for researchers and policymakers to reason about technical and substantive difficulties in both objectives. They identify mismatches between desired outcomes and feasible implementations, arguing that these explain why unlearning is not a general-purpose way to constrain generative-model behavior. The practical contribution is a clearer basis for evaluating an unlearning proposal against the particular change it is meant to achieve.
neurips-2025-machine-unlearning-doesn-t-.tldr: The paper distinguishes removing learned information from suppressing outputs and explains why unlearning cannot generally fulfill every proposed policy goal.

paragraphs: Updating a deployed language model requires adding or correcting knowledge while preserving previous information and core capabilities. Repeated edits make this harder because changes can interfere with one another. MEMOIR addresses long sequences of edits using a dedicated residual memory module.

During editing, data-dependent masks make input activations sparse and confine each change to a distinct subset of memory parameters. This limits overlap among edits. At inference time, the framework compares a query's sparse activation pattern with patterns stored during editing, identifying which changes are relevant. This supports rephrased queries while suppressing unnecessary memory activation for unrelated prompts.

Experiments with LLaMA-3 and Mistral cover question answering, hallucination correction, and out-of-distribution generalization. The authors report state-of-the-art reliability, generalization, and locality results, with thousands of sequential edits and minimal forgetting. The contribution combines selective writing with selective retrieval: limiting where an edit is stored helps preserve earlier updates, while identifying when it should activate helps make that knowledge useful without unnecessarily affecting other responses.
neurips-2025-memoir-lifelong-model-editi.tldr: MEMOIR stores edits in sparse residual memory and selectively activates relevant changes, supporting thousands of updates with minimal forgetting.

paragraphs: Pause tokens are filler symbols that can improve Transformer performance without themselves supplying substantive task content. This paper gives a formal explanation for their computational effect. It studies Transformers whose depth is constant and whose width grows logarithmically, showing that adding pause tokens strictly increases expressivity.

For bounded-precision activations, models without pause tokens can compute only a strict subset of the function class AC⁰. Adding a polynomial number of pause tokens enables the complete class. Under logarithmic precision, pause tokens enable expressivity equivalent to TC⁰, matching known upper bounds. These statements depend on the specified depth, width, precision, and pause-token settings.

An empirical study also shows that two-layer causally masked Transformers can learn parity with pause tokens, while they appear unable to learn it without them. The experiment complements the formal separation without turning that observed learning difficulty into an unrestricted impossibility claim. Together, the results establish pause tokens as a computational mechanism that complements chain-of-thought prompting and clarify how their effects interact with architectural constraints.
neurips-2025-pause-tokens-strictly-incre.tldr: Under specified width and precision constraints, pause tokens provably expand what constant-depth Transformers can compute.

paragraphs: Predicting an individual's choices requires combining numerical considerations, such as cost and time, with preferences and constraints expressed in language. A prediction suited to a population may miss this individual variation. ATHENA addresses the problem by joining symbolic utility modeling with language-based personalization.

The framework has two stages. First, language-model-assisted symbolic discovery identifies robust utility functions at the group level. Second, individual semantic adaptation builds personalized textual templates guided by those utility functions. This connects a structured account of trade-offs with the language that describes a particular person's situation and preferences.

Tests on real-world travel-mode and vaccine-choice tasks report improvements over utility-based, machine-learning, and other language-model approaches. The abstract states an F1 improvement of at least 6.5% over the strongest competing models. Removing either stage reduces predictive performance, supporting their complementary roles. The findings concern modeling observed choices: they show the benefit of combining shared utility structure with individual semantic context when predicting decisions.
neurips-2025-personalized-decision-model.tldr: ATHENA combines group-level symbolic utility functions with individual language-based adaptation to improve personalized choice prediction.

paragraphs: ShapeLLM-Omni extends multimodal language modeling to understanding and generating 3D assets alongside text. Its intended capability is to handle both forms of content in any sequence. This requires a representation of 3D objects that can fit into the model's token-based processing.

The authors first train a 3D vector-quantized variational autoencoder. It maps objects into discrete latent representations while supporting efficient, accurate shape reconstruction. These discrete 3D tokens provide the foundation for 3D-Alpaca, a large training dataset covering generation, comprehension, and editing. The dataset brings several forms of 3D interaction into a common training resource.

Finally, the authors instruction-tune Qwen-2.5-vl-7B-Instruct on 3D-Alpaca to equip it with native 3D understanding and generation. The contribution is a complete route from shape representation to training data to a multimodal model. The abstract presents this as an effective step toward 3D intelligence, with the representation and dataset also supplying resources for further work on language models that handle three-dimensional content.
neurips-2025-shapellm-omni-a-native-mult.tldr: ShapeLLM-Omni combines discrete 3D tokens, a new instruction dataset, and model fine-tuning to understand and generate text and 3D assets.

paragraphs: High-dimensional optimization problems can have entire smooth sets of minimizers because of symmetries or overparameterization. When this solution structure is known, at least locally, it can guide how the problem is parameterized. This paper studies reduction mappings that use such knowledge to remove redundant directions.

These mappings reparameterize part of the parameter space to lie on the solution manifold and naturally arise from inner optimization problems. The result is a lower-dimensional objective. The authors develop a general framework for understanding how the reduction changes the geometry of that objective, rather than treating dimension reduction alone as an explanation for faster optimization.

The analysis shows that well-designed reductions improve curvature and conditioning, leading to theoretically faster convergence for gradient-based methods. The result depends on the quality of the reduction and available structural information; it does not say every reparameterization helps. By bringing several scenarios into one framework, the paper offers a principled explanation for empirical acceleration seen when optimization methods exploit structure at their solutions.
neurips-2025-sharper-convergence-rates-f.tldr: Well-designed reduction mappings exploit known solution geometry to improve conditioning and accelerate gradient-based nonconvex optimization.

paragraphs: Key-value caching reduces repeated computation during language-model inference, but the stored information can consume substantial GPU memory as tasks become larger and more complex. The paper focuses on resource-constrained edge servers, where reducing cache size through additional computation can itself be costly.

Sim-LLM uses similarity between tasks to reuse cached keys and values from tasks already processed. Subsequent similar tasks can draw on this stored information during inference. This makes reuse across tasks the central optimization, with the aim of reducing memory consumption while allowing larger batches and increasing throughput.

Evaluations on A40 and A100 GPUs report throughput improvements of up to 39.40% and memory reductions of up to 34.65% compared with state-of-the-art approaches, with minimal accuracy degradation. These are reported maximum gains rather than uniform improvements for every workload. The results show that task similarity can provide a useful source of cache reuse and that the resulting memory savings can translate into greater system capacity in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2025-sim-llm-optimizing-llm-infe.tldr: Sim-LLM reuses key-value caches across similar tasks to reduce GPU memory use and increase inference throughput with minimal accuracy degradation.

paragraphs: When an agent cannot directly observe the full state of its environment, choosing actions may require using a history of observations. One training strategy gives an expert access to the hidden state and teaches the agent to imitate that expert. This can be computationally efficient, but it also has known failure modes.

The paper compares this privileged expert distillation with reinforcement learning that lacks privileged state information. It uses a theoretical model called the perturbed Block MDP and controlled experiments on simulated locomotion tasks. The analysis contrasts approximate decodability with belief contraction to predict how randomness in the hidden dynamics affects the trade-off.

The experiments support stochasticity as a central factor in that trade-off. A second finding is that the best policy for an expert with hidden-state access is not always the best policy to teach a partially observing agent. These results suggest that selecting a teacher requires considering what the student can learn from its available information, and they provide guidance for exploiting privileged training information more effectively.
neurips-2025-to-distill-or-decide-unders.tldr: The value of privileged expert distillation depends on hidden-dynamics stochasticity, and the optimal fully informed expert is not always the best teacher.

paragraphs: Assessing a video's aesthetics involves more than applying image assessment to individual frames. Video changes over time, and combining its different information sources creates additional challenges. The paper identifies a shortage of standardized data and strong models as obstacles to progress in this area.

VADB addresses the data problem with 10,490 diverse videos annotated by 37 professionals. Its annotations include overall aesthetic scores, scores for particular attributes, written comments, and objective tags. This provides several ways to describe the same video, connecting numerical judgments with more detailed language and attribute information. The authors describe VADB as the largest video aesthetic database.

The paper also introduces VADB-Net, a dual-modal pretraining framework with two training stages. It outperforms existing video quality assessment models on scoring tasks and supports downstream aesthetic assessment tasks. Together, the database and model provide resources for learning and evaluating video aesthetics across multiple dimensions. The contribution pairs richer professional judgments with a framework designed to use multimodal information for prediction.
neurips-2025-vadb-a-large-scale-video-ae.tldr: VADB supplies professional multidimensional annotations for 10,490 videos and a dual-modal model that improves aesthetic scoring.

paragraphs: Vision-language models can generalize well without task-specific examples, yet adapting them with limited supervision remains difficult. Fixed prompts shared across inputs offer limited flexibility for individual examples and uncertainty. VaMP makes prompt learning depend on the current sample and models prompts probabilistically.

The framework samples input-conditioned prompts from a learned posterior distribution. It also constructs a class-aware prior using both the instance representation and a class prototype, connecting information about the particular example with broader class structure. Prompt tuning is formulated as variational inference over latent prompts, and reparameterized sampling enables the whole framework to train end to end.

Experiments on few-shot learning and domain generalization benchmarks report state-of-the-art performance. The results support the combination of sample-specific adaptation, uncertainty modeling, and class information in the evaluated tasks. The method's central contribution is to treat a prompt as a learned distribution conditioned on the input, giving adaptation a way to represent variation that a single fixed prompt cannot capture.
neurips-2025-vamp-variational-multi-moda.tldr: VaMP learns input-conditioned prompt distributions with class-aware priors to improve few-shot adaptation and domain generalization.
